### 2026-10-09 – I worked on the firmware for my keychain version of starbie, a sparkle-shaped board with my own cat art. I did the coding on arduino i'll probably edit and add more code later, still not feeling reall

**2h**

I worked on the firmware for my keychain version of starbie, a sparkle-shaped board with my own cat art. I did the coding on arduino i'll probably edit and add more code later, still not feeling really good about it, but i'll just state the stuff i added so far.

What I changed:

Fixed the  pins to match my board. My schematic wires D4 to SCL and D5 to SDA, but the code expected the opposite. i swapped I2C_SDA_PIN and I2C_SCL_PIN to 7 and 6 so the screen and tilt sensor will work with my wiring.

renamed the menu to fit my cat theme: FEED became SNACK and PET became PURR

Added a sparkle trail behind the pet, redrawn as a plus star shape to suit my cat. I edited the pixel coordinates in drawSparkle and added the call under the pet's drawBitmap line.

I drew a cat, converted it to a 32 x 32 byte array with image2cpp, and pasted it into PET_SPRITE.

Added a shake-for-a-fortune feature.It has a list of my own messages, and a new drawFortune function that shows a message box when the board is shaken.

Problems I solved:

Arduino gave a "Missing FQBN" error, so I installed the ESP32 board package and selected XIAO_ESP32C3. This took me some time to figure out because i didn't really know what i was doing in th beginning
My first sprite paste broke the compile because I pasted image2cpp's whole output inside the array. I fixed it by pasting only the bytes between the braces. Had to ask for some help on this one but got it working soon.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/91GnKkybMzvrVrYZKu3nkMqr3A05rf5g/8e79443c670a756b31c9041ea949ef97b243e4e6b1df088f63b051cb5ee2777b.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/91GnKkybMzvrVrYZKu3nkMqr3A05rf5g/6dffd915040244586ac51ead75663401c2d3ecd45d0031a74e35a99fe045319d.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/91GnKkybMzvrVrYZKu3nkMqr3A05rf5g/c59fdbb729eadcd9cf29dba24c8f815d4bf7193d8086ec714c53f71aff70024c.png)

Overall, i had a super hard time with this. Coding in general always gave me a bit of a headache and it took me a while to understand why I was getting errors and how to fix them, and to understand the code as well. Hopefully the changes I made work!!

### 2026-10-09 – I added some morefeatures to the firmware. Coding still continues to bethe most difficult thing in the world to me.

**1h**

I added some morefeatures to the firmware. Coding still continues to bethe most difficult thing in the world to me.

Temperature mood-->
added HOT_TEMP_C and COLD_TEMP_C settings so the cat reacts to the room temperature

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/91GnKkybMzvrVrYZKu3nkMqr3A05rf5g/45e34e1fa4e16db53586ea2f1ba3d5cb49363578f42ee73531428c5909d6fcc9.png)

wrote a drawWeatherMood function that reads temperatureC. When it's hot, a sweat drop slides down the cat and "hot!" appears. when it's cold, "brr" appears. It does nothing if there's no reading yet or the cat is asleep.

Startup screen:

Wrote a showStartup function that shows the cat's name (celeste) for 2 seconds with a twinkling star effect, built from 8 frames of 250 ms each. it reuses my star-shaped drawSparkle.
called it in setup() right before the first screen draw.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/91GnKkybMzvrVrYZKu3nkMqr3A05rf5g/c740ff786cd09621f9c5aac3e331ce3ca31b88b43cb958e782436dfd3a7c804b.png)

wrote the code in arduino ide for a while for this until I remembered to record coding time with hackatime and  write it in vs code bcs it has the extension so copy-pasted it there and completed it and then compiled it in arduino ide. does that make sense? I don't know if i'm using the right words.
i added a screen saver to my firmware and fixed three bugs that i encountered.---->

added two settings, in which the screen dims after 30 seconds and the screen turns off after 2 minutes.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 190833](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/91GnKkybMzvrVrYZKu3nkMqr3A05rf5g/3d13f9032bd2def7729e4dd6a07fab445879d6586f8fb03cd239ea89d36402ed.png)

added three variables to track the last activity time and whether the screen is dimmed or off.
added wakeScreen(), which resets the idle timer and undoes dimming or turning off using the

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 203249](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/91GnKkybMzvrVrYZKu3nkMqr3A05rf5g/e81a8696af2bab62d920cac947a7f7a9614e1fff9336fac5944ea2c09252420a.png)
Bugs I fixed---->

Tangled brackets in handleButtons()-->VS Code was showing  red brackets, and  it was too much work trying to figure out which ones to delete so i ended up rewriting the whole function and I replaced it with a clean one
'now' was not declared in this scope: the line lastShakeAt = now; had ended up in loop(), where now doesn't exist. I removed it and put wakeScreen() inside checkForShake(), where now is defined.

Inverted sprite: i learnt that my pet sprite was gonna be on a dark background so I re-ran my 32 x 32 image through image2cpp with "Invert image colors" on, and pasted in only the new bytes.

### 2026-10-10 – I added a second pet sprite to my Starbie firmware, so my cat looks different while it naps.

**0.38h**

I added a second pet sprite to my Starbie firmware, so my cat looks different while it naps.

Converted my sleepy cat image with image2cpp (32 x 32, horizontal 1 bit per pixel, invert colors on)

Pasted the bytes into a new array called SLEEP_SPRITE, placed right below PET_SPRITE in the settings block. (took me a while to figure out where to place it)
Changed drawPet(). Now the cat switches to the sleepy sprite when I choose NAP, and switches back when it wakes naturally or when I shake it. (hopefully)
then i verified it by compiling it in arduino ide and using the verify option
